newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus falls 32.4 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus falls 32.4 percent in 1996.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus fell 32.4 percent in calendar 1996 from the previous year to 6.74 trillion yen, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
The merchandise trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, declined 16.5 percent to 3.55 trillion yen in 1996 from the previous year.
At Thursday's exchange rate, the overall trade surplus was $56.6 billion and the surplus with the United States was $29.8 billion.

In December alone, Japan's trade surplus fell 20.6 percent from a year earlier to 881.48 billion yen ($7.40 billion). The merchandise trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 7.8 percent in December from a year earlier to 389.11 billion yen ($3.26 billion). The figures are issued only in yen.

Economists polled by Reuters had predicted an average fall of about 7.4 percent to 1.029 trillion yen ($8.6 billion) for the overall December figure. But some had said the trade surplus might rise due to a surge in car exports stemming from the depreciation of the yen, which makes Japanese exports more competitive abroad.
Japan's trade surplus rose 0.2 percent in November from a year earlier to 675.19 billion yen ($5.67 billion), the first time in two years it had risen on a year-on-year basis. ($1=119 yen)
